त्यसपछि उनी रिहा भएकी हुन्।

एमाले अध्यक्ष केपी शर्मा ओलीले प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाहको भारत भ्रमणलाई उपलब्धिविहीन भन्दै आलोचना गरेका छन्। उनले प्रधानमन्त्रीले भ्रमणअघि राजनीतिक दल तथा सरोकारवालासँग छलफल नगरेको र राष्ट्रिय मुद्दामा साझा धारणा बनाउन नसकेको आरोप लगाए।

सम्पादकहरूसँग बिहीबार भएको संवादमा ओलीले बालेनले विगतमा ग्रेटर नेपालको नक्सा महानगरको कार्यकक्षमा राखे पनि भारत भ्रमणमा सीमा विवादको विषय नउठाएको दाबी गरे। प्रधानमन्त्रीको भ्रमणमा सिंगो राष्ट्रको प्रतिनिधित्व हुनुपर्नेमा त्यो निजी भ्रमणजस्तो देखिएको उनको टिप्पणी थियो।

ओलीले भारतसँग भएका सहमतिलाई नयाँ उपलब्धिका रूपमा प्रस्तुत गर्न नमिल्ने बताए। विगतमा घोषणा भएका सहायता रकमसमेत प्राप्त नभएको उल्लेख गर्दै उनले अहिले घोषणा गरिएको विकास सहायता कार्यान्वयन हुनेमा पनि सावधानी अपनाउनुपर्ने धारणा राखे।

ईपीजीसम्बन्धी विषयमा सरकारको अडानप्रति असन्तुष्टि जनाएका ओलीले प्रेसमाथि सरकारी व्यवहार, न्यायालयको कार्यसम्पादन र संवैधानिक निकायको भूमिकाबारे पनि प्रश्न उठाए। लोकतन्त्र र प्रेस स्वतन्त्रताको रक्षाका लागि प्रतिवाद आवश्यक रहेको उनको भनाइ थियो।

उनले स्थानीय र प्रदेश निर्वाचन एकैसाथ गर्न नहुने धारणा राख्दै संविधानले तोकेको अवधिअनुसार छुट्टाछुट्टै निर्वाचन हुनुपर्ने तर्क गरे। एमालेले लोकतन्त्र पुनःस्थापनाका लागि आन्दोलन आवश्यक रहेको बताउँदै आएको भए पनि अहिले लोकतन्त्र नरहेको भन्ने प्रश्नको जवाफ भने नदिएको समाचारमा उल्लेख छ।

पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री डा. बाबुराम भट्टराईले राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा)प्रति आफ्नो सद्भाव र समर्थन रहेको बताएका छन्। संविधान जारी भएपछि सुरु गरेको वैकल्पिक राजनीतिक अभियानको एउटा प्रमुख धारका रूपमा अहिले रास्वपा उदाएको उनको भनाइ छ।

तर, नयाँ राजनीतिक शक्तिहरूले सत्तामा पुगेपछि मात्रै उपलब्धि ठान्न नहुने भन्दै भट्टराईले इतिहास र लोकतान्त्रिक आन्दोलनको योगदानलाई भुल्न नहुने सुझाव दिएका छन्। मुलुकका गम्भीर आर्थिक र भूराजनीतिक चुनौती समाधान गर्न नयाँ पुस्ता जिम्मेवार बन्नुपर्ने उनले बताए।

भट्टराईले सत्तापक्षले आफूलाई स्थायी शासक ठान्ने, प्रतिपक्षले सरकार ढाल्न मात्रै ध्यान दिने र सञ्चारमाध्यम उत्तेजक विषयमा केन्द्रित हुने प्रवृत्तिले मुलुकलाई संकटतर्फ धकेल्न सक्ने चेतावनी दिए।

प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाहले विद्यमान संविधानको व्यवस्थाअनुसार संसदीय लोकतन्त्रप्रति उत्तरदायी हुँदै संसद् र राजनीतिक दलहरूसँग सहकार्य गर्नुपर्ने उनको भनाइ छ। सरकारको आन्तरिक व्यवस्थापन कमजोर भई आर्थिक विकास र सुशासनमा असफल भए जनतामा निराशा बढ्ने र त्यसको असर समग्र लोकतान्त्रिक व्यवस्थामा पर्ने उनले बताए।

लामो समयदेखि बन्द रहेको नेपालको पहिलो आधुनिक उद्योग विराटनगर जुट मिल्स पुनः सञ्चालनमा ल्याउन सरकारले प्रक्रिया अघि बढाएको छ। विराटनगर र दमकमा रहेको ६७ बिघा औद्योगिक जग्गा उपयोग गर्दै सार्वजनिक–निजी साझेदारीमार्फत उद्योग सञ्चालन गर्ने तयारी गरिएको हो।

सरकारले स्वदेशी तथा विदेशी लगानीकर्ताबाट आशयपत्र आह्वान गरेको छ। छनोट भएका लगानीकर्तालाई ३५ वर्षसम्म उद्योग सञ्चालन गर्न दिने योजना रहेको छ।

उद्योग पुनः सञ्चालनमा आएपछि करिब ५ हजार जनालाई रोजगारी दिने लक्ष्य राखिएको छ। यसबाट स्वदेशी उत्पादन बढाउन, आयात घटाउन तथा औद्योगिक क्षेत्रको विकासमा सहयोग पुग्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

प्रतिष्ठानले पारित गरेको विस्तारित स्वास्थ्य सेवा कार्यविधि २०८३ अनुसार यो सेवा सुरु गर्न लागिएको उपकुलपति प्राडा अजय मिश्रले जानकारी दिए । यस निर्णयबाट दाङसहित रोल्पा, रुकुम, सल्यान र प्यूठानका सर्वसाधारणलाई स्वास्थ्य उपचारमा सहजता पुग्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ । नियमित समयमा अस्पताल पुग्न नसक्ने र बिदाका दिन उपचार चाहिने बिरामीलाई विशेष राहत पुग्ने प्रतिष्ठानको भनाइ छ ।

शशांक कोइरालासँग खोजे समर्थन
-
बुधबार चुनदेवीस्थित सम्पर्क कार्यालयमा महाधिवेशन तयारी समितिको बैठक बस्नुअघि निधि र कोइरालाबीच भेटवार्ता भएको थियो।

नेता शशांक कोइराला पनि सभापति पदका आकांक्षी हुन्।

निधिले समर्थन खोज्दा  के भने कोइरालाले?

पर्यटन बोर्ड सीईओ छनोटविरुद्ध
सर्वोच्चको कारण देखाऊ आदेश

काठमाडौं । नेपाल पर्यटन बोर्डको प्रमुख कार्यकारी अधिकृत (सीईओ) छनोटविरुद्ध सर्वोच्च अदालतमा परेको रिटमा सर्वोच्चले कारण देखाऊ आदेश जारी गरेको छ । न्यायाधीश रत्नबहादुर बागचन्दको एकल इजलासले विपक्षीबाट १५ दिनभित्र महान्यायाधिवक्ताको कार्यालयमार्फत लिखित जवाफ मागेको छ । अन्तरिम आदेशबारे दुवै पक्षबीच छलफल गर्न मंसिर १४ गते पेसी तोकिएको छ ।

निवेदकहरूले १६ जनाको संक्षिप्त सूचीका आधारमा अघि बढाइएको छनोट प्रक्रिया पर्यटन बोर्ड ऐन, कर्मचारी सेवा विनियमावली र छनोट कार्यविधिविपरीत रहेको दाबी गरेका छन् । ऐनले सीईओका लागि स्नातकोत्तर उपाधिसहित पर्यटन क्षेत्रमा कम्तीमा १० वर्षको अनुभव तोकेको छ, तर केही उम्मेदवारको अनुभव त्यो मापदण्ड नपुगेको र छनोट पारदर्शी नभएको उनीहरूको जिकिर छ ।

बसुन्धरादेखि सामाखुशीस्थित रेडन पुलसम्म खोलाको दायाँबायाँ करिडोर निर्माण भइरहेको छ।

तीन वर्षअघि काठमाडौं महानगरपालिकाले सामाखुशी खोलामाथि बनाइएका स्ल्याब तथा आसपासका अवैध संरचना हटाएको थियो।

महिला हिंसा अन्त्य कहिले ?
नारामा होइन, व्यवहारमा

काठमाडौं । हरेक वर्ष नोभेम्बर २५ देखि डिसेम्बर १० सम्म विश्वभर लैङ्गिक हिंसाविरुद्धको १६ दिने अभियान मनाइन्छ । तर यो अभियान नारामा मात्र सीमित हुनु हुँदैन, महिला हिंसाको अन्त्य व्यवहारमै देखिनुपर्छ भन्ने आवाज उठेको छ ।

नेपाल जनसाङ्ख्यिक तथा स्वास्थ्य सर्वेक्षण २०२२ अनुसार १५ देखि ४९ वर्ष उमेर समूहका २३ प्रतिशत महिलाले १५ वर्षको उमेरपछि कुनै न कुनै शारीरिक हिंसा भोगेका छन् । हिंसा भोगेकामध्ये ५८ प्रतिशतले न सहयोग खोजे, न कसैलाई आफ्नो पीडा सुनाए । हिंसा देखेर मौन बस्ने र पीडितलाई नै दोष दिने प्रवृत्ति अन्त्य गर्नुपर्नेमा जोड दिइएको छ ।

राष्ट्रिय खेलकुदमा बागमती
दोस्रो दिन पनि शीर्ष स्थानमा

सुर्खेत । दशौँ राष्ट्रिय खेलकुद प्रतियोगिताको दोस्रो दिनको पदक तालिकामा बागमती प्रदेश शीर्ष स्थानमा रहेको छ । वीरेन्द्रनगरस्थित रंगशालामा बुधबार भएका खेलपछि बागमतीले ९ स्वर्ण, ४ रजत र ६ कास्य गरी कुल १९ पदक जितेको छ ।

दोस्रो स्थानमा एनआरएनए रहेको छ, जसले ६ स्वर्णसहित ९ पदक जितेको छ । नेपाल प्रहरी १८ पदकसहित तेस्रो स्थानमा छ भने नेपाली सेनाले पनि १८ पदक जितेको छ । सुदूरपश्चिमले ३ र कोशीले १ पदक जितेका छन्, तर एपीएफ, गण्डकी, कर्णाली, लुम्बिनी र मधेसले अझै पदक जित्न सकेका छैनन् ।

कार्कीले अन्तरिम आदेश पाएनन्
मनोज केसीलाई बाटो खुला

काठमाडौं । सर्वोच्च अदालतले आईजीपीबाट हटाइएका दानबहादुर कार्कीको मागबमोजिम अन्तरिम आदेश दिन अश्वीकार गरेको छ । न्यायाधीश श्रीकान्त पौडेल र नृपध्वज निरौलाको संयुक्त इजलासमा दिनभरिको बहसपछि अन्तरिम आदेश जारी नहुने ठहर भएको हो । यो आदेशसँगै डा. मनोज केसीलाई आईजीपीका रूपमा काम गर्ने बाटो अदालतबाट पनि खुला भएको छ ।

सरकारले कात्तिक १८ गते कार्कीलाई प्रहरी महानिरीक्षकको जिम्मेवारीबाट हटाएर प्रधानमन्त्रीको विशेष सुरक्षा सल्लाहकारमा सरुवा गर्दै एआईजी डा. मनोजकुमार केसीलाई आईजीपीमा बढुवा गरेको थियो । आफूलाई गैरकानुनी रूपमा पदमुक्त गरेको दाबी गर्दै कार्कीले कात्तिक २० गते सर्वोच्चमा रिट दायर गरेका थिए ।

इजिप्टको राजधानी कायरोमा इन्धन बोकेको ट्यांकर दुर्घटनापछि भएको भीषण आगलागीमा परी कम्तीमा ३१ जनाको मृत्यु भएको छ भने २१ जना घाइते भएका छन्।

बुधबार साँझ कायरोको वर्राक क्षेत्रमा पर्ने रिङ रोडमा इन्धन बोकेको ट्यांकर दुर्घटनामा परेपछि आगलागी भएको हो। ट्यांकरमा लागेको आगो आसपासबाट गुज्रिरहेका अन्य सवारीसाधनमा समेत फैलिँदा ठूलो क्षति भएको बताइएको छ।

इजिप्टको स्वास्थ्य मन्त्रालयका अनुसार घाइतेमध्ये केहीको शरीर जलेको छ भने केहीलाई आगलागीबाट निस्किएको धुवाँका कारण श्वासप्रश्वासमा समस्या भएको छ। उनीहरूलाई नजिकका अस्पतालमा लगेर उपचार भइरहेको छ।

सामाजिक सञ्जालमा सार्वजनिक भएका भिडियोहरूमा राजमार्गमा आगोका ठूला लप्का उठिरहेको र आकाशभरि बाक्लो कालो धुवाँ फैलिएको देखिन्छ। आगलागीका कारण आसपासमा रहेका कैयौँ सवारीसाधन जलेर नष्ट भएका छन्।

सरकारी अखबार अल–अहरामका अनुसार प्रारम्भिक अनुसन्धानमा ट्यांकर अगाडि उच्च भोल्टेजको विद्युत् तार खसेपछि चालकले सवारीसाधनमाथिको नियन्त्रण गुमाएको पाइएको छ।

त्यसपछि ट्यांकर सडकको डिभाइडर पार गर्दै पल्टिएको र त्यसबाट पेट्रोल सडकमा पोखिएपछि आगलागी भएको प्रारम्भिक विवरणमा उल्लेख छ।

घटनाको वास्तविक कारण तथा दुर्घटनाको विस्तृत विवरण पत्ता लगाउन सम्बन्धित अधिकारीहरूले थप अनुसन्धान गरिरहेका छन्।

कांग्रेसमा ११ महिला नेतृ
केन्द्रीय सदस्यमा मनोनीत

काठमाडौं । नेपाली कांग्रेसले सुजाता कोइरालासहित ११ जना महिला नेतालाई केन्द्रीय सदस्यमा मनोनीत गरेको छ । सानेपामा जारी केन्द्रीय समिति बैठकले मनोनीत गर्ने निर्णय गरेपछि सूची निर्वाचन आयोगमा पठाइएको छ ।

२३१ सदस्यीय निर्वाचित केन्द्रीय समितिमा एक तिहाइ महिला पुर्‍याउन ११ जना अपुग भएकाले महाधिवेशनमा प्रतिस्पर्धा नगरेका ११ जनालाई मनोनीत गरिएको हो । मनोनीत हुनेमा कोइरालासहित ईश्वरी न्यौपाने, चन्दा चौधरी, लक्ष्मी पाण्डे, साहजान खातुन र निपा चोख्याल छन् भने अन्य पाँच जनाको नाम अझै खुलेको छैन ।

राप्रपा महाधिवेशन : अध्यक्षमा थापा कि पाण्डे ?

काठमाडौं । राष्ट्रिय प्रजातन्त्र पार्टी (राप्रपा)को आठौं महाधिवेशन नजिकिँदै गर्दा अध्यक्ष पदको प्रतिस्पर्धा रोचक बनेको छ । अध्यक्षमा दोहोरिन चाहेका राजेन्द्र लिङ्देनलाई रोक्न पूर्वअध्यक्ष कमल थापा र डा. प्रकाशचन्द्र लोहनी एक ठाउँ उभिएका छन् ।

महाधिवेशन मंसिर २६, २७ र २८ गते काठमाडौंमा हुँदैछ । संस्थापनइतर पक्षबाट थापा वा विक्रम पाण्डेमध्ये एकले उम्मेदवारी दिने निश्चितजस्तै छ । पाण्डेले सर्वसम्मत नेतृत्व चयनको पक्षमा रहेको बताएका छन् भने प्रवक्ता ज्ञानेन्द्रबहादुर शाहीले अध्यक्ष पदमा उम्मेदवारी घोषणा गरिसकेका छन् ।

गगन नेतृत्वको कार्यसमितिलाई आयोगको औपचारिक मान्यता

काठमाडौं । नेपाली कांग्रेसका सभापति गगन थापाले निर्वाचन आयोगले १५औँ महाधिवेशनबाट निर्वाचित नयाँ केन्द्रीय कार्यसमितिलाई अद्यावधिक गरेको जानकारी पार्टी बैठकलाई गराएका छन्। सानेपामा बसेको केन्द्रीय समिति बैठकमा थापाले आयोगबाट कार्यसमिति अद्यावधिक भएको पत्र प्राप्त भएको बताए।

महाधिवेशनले पारित गरेको संशोधित विधान र राजनीतिक दस्ताबेजलाई पनि आयोगले औपचारिक रूपमा अद्यावधिक गरेको छ। यससँगै थापा नेतृत्वको २३१ सदस्यीय कार्यसमितिले संस्थागत अभिलेखमा पूर्ण वैधानिकता पाएको छ। यद्यपि देउवा समूहले पनि समानान्तर महाधिवेशन गर्ने जानकारी आयोगलाई गराएको छ।

खगेन्द्र सुनारको साइबर मुद्दा
प्रमाण सुनारलाई देखाउन आदेश

काठमाडौं । काभ्रेपलाञ्चोक जिल्ला अदालतले रास्वपा सांसद खगेन्द्र सुनारविरुद्धको साइबर अपराध मुद्दामा जाहेरवाला मनिषा गौतमले पुनः पेस गरेका प्रमाणहरूको जानकारी प्रतिवादी सुनारलाई गराउन आदेश दिएको छ। जिल्ला न्यायाधीश माधवप्रसाद मैनालीको इजलासले बुधबार सुनुवाइ गर्दै उक्त आदेश जारी गरेको हो।

यसअघि प्रहरी र सरकारी वकिलमार्फत अदालतमा पेस गरिएका अडियो लगायतका प्रमाण अदालतबाटै हराएका थिए। त्यसपछि जाहेरवाला गौतमले गत असोज १५ गते निवेदनसहित अडियो तथा अन्य प्रमाण सरकारी वकिल कार्यालयमार्फत पुनः पेस गरेकी थिइन्।

महिला क्रिकेटमा कोशीको पहिलो जित

सुर्खेत । दशौँ राष्ट्रिय खेलकुद प्रतियोगिताअन्तर्गत महिला क्रिकेटमा कोशी प्रदेशले पहिलो जित निकालेको छ । बुधबार भएको खेलमा कोशीले कर्णाली प्रदेशलाई ४९ रनले पराजित गर्‍यो ।

The moment was captured in a video recorded at Nvidia's headquarters in Santa Clara, California, on Monday, November 23, and later shared on X.

During his address, Huang expressed regret over putting employees through the difficult situation.

"I'm terribly sorry for putting you through all of this," he told staff.

As he spoke, a female employee approached him and embraced him. Other employees gathered in the lobby could be heard cheering and applauding during the exchange. The staff member has not been publicly identified.

Huang also acknowledged making "some very terrible mistakes" and thanked employees for giving him another opportunity to lead the company.

"I'm going to be a better CEO the second time around," he said.

Why Did Jensen Huang Leave Nvidia?
Huang's departure followed a personal controversy after he admitted to having an affair. Reports also emerged suggesting that he may have been targeted by a Chinese intelligence operation, prompting Nvidia's board to launch an investigation.

On November 23, Nvidia announced that Huang had been reinstated as president, CEO and a member of its board, just 11 days after his resignation was announced.

The company's board said the decision was unanimous and followed discussions with Huang, along with input from senior US government officials.

Investigation Still Underway
Despite Huang's return, questions surrounding the reported foreign intelligence operation remain unresolved.

Nvidia confirmed that its investigation into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort would continue.

The company has also established a dedicated board committee to oversee national security and export-control risks. Additionally, Nvidia is searching for a chief compliance officer to strengthen its compliance oversight.

Huang's emotional interaction with employees has since drawn attention online, adding a human moment to one of the most unexpected leadership comebacks in the technology industry.

प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाहले आफ्नो पहिलो भारत भ्रमणका क्रममा विगतका प्रधानमन्त्रीहरूले अपनाउँदै आएको केही परम्परा तोडेका छन्। उनले नयाँदिल्लीस्थित नेपाली दूतावासको भ्रमण गरेनन् भने भारतमा रहेका प्रवासी नेपालीहरूसँग पनि प्रत्यक्ष भेटघाट गरेनन्।

प्रधानमन्त्री शाहको मंसिर ६ र ७ गते भएको दुईदिने भारत भ्रमणका क्रममा दूतावासले आयोजना गर्ने परम्परागत स्वागत समारोह (रिसेप्सन) समेत राखिएन। यसअघिका अधिकांश प्रधानमन्त्रीले भारतको राजकीय भ्रमणका क्रममा नेपाली दूतावास पुगेर नेपाली तथा भारतीय विशिष्ट व्यक्तिहरूसँग भेटघाट गर्ने र स्वागत समारोहमा सहभागी हुने गरेका थिए।

भारतका लागि नेपालका निवर्तमान राजदूत डा. शंकर शर्माका अनुसार यसअघिका प्रधानमन्त्रीहरूको भ्रमणमा दूतावासले स्वागत समारोह आयोजना गर्ने गरेको थियो। उक्त कार्यक्रममा भारतीय उच्च अधिकारी, पूर्वमुख्यमन्त्री, सेवानिवृत्त कर्मचारी तथा प्रवासी नेपालीहरू सहभागी हुने गर्थे।

तर, परराष्ट्र मन्त्रालयले यसपटकको भ्रमणलाई मुख्य कार्यसूचीमा केन्द्रित गरिएको जनाएको छ। प्रधानमन्त्री शाहको प्राथमिकता भारतीय प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदीसँगको द्विपक्षीय वार्तालाई सफल बनाउनु रहेकाले दूतावास भ्रमण र स्वागत समारोहको कार्यक्रम नराखिएको परराष्ट्र अधिकारीहरूको भनाइ छ।

प्रधानमन्त्रीकी मिडिया व्यवस्थापन संयोजक दीपा दाहालले पनि समयको सीमितता र भ्रमणको छोटो कार्यतालिकाका कारण दूतावासको स्वागत समारोह नराखिएको बताएकी छन्।

यस क्रममा भारतस्थित राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी निकट प्रवासी नेपाली सम्पर्क मञ्चका पदाधिकारीले समेत प्रधानमन्त्रीसँग प्रत्यक्ष भेटघाट गर्न पाएनन्। मञ्चका अध्यक्ष अर्जुनप्रसाद भण्डारीले प्रधानमन्त्रीसँग प्रत्यक्ष भेट हुन नसकेको तर सचिवालयका सदस्यहरूसँग कुराकानी भएको बताएका छन्।

त्यस्तै, भारतमा रहेका अन्य चार नेपाली संगठनले पनि प्रधानमन्त्रीसँग भेटेर आफ्ना समस्या राख्न समय नपाएको गुनासो गरेका छन्।

मूल प्रवाह अखिल भारत नेपाली एकता समाज, नेपाली समाज भारत, प्रवासी नेपाली संघ भारत र जनसम्पर्क समिति भारतले संयुक्त रूपमा सातबुँदे ज्ञापनपत्र सार्वजनिक गरेका छन्।

उनीहरूले प्रधानमन्त्रीसँग भेटका लागि समय माग्दै ज्ञापनपत्र तयार पारे पनि प्रधानमन्त्रीको कार्यालय र नयाँदिल्लीस्थित नेपाली दूतावासबाट समय उपलब्ध नभएपछि सार्वजनिक गर्नुपरेको बताएका छन्।

A HEARTBREAKING REMINDER THAT OCEAN TRASH CAN KILL. 💔🦈

A juvenile reef shark was found dead floating near Sta. Cruz Island in Zamboanga City, Philippines, on November 19, 2025, with a disposable diaper wrapped around its head.

Diver Harvey Yap believed the diaper may have caused the young shark to suffocate. The Department of Environment and Natural Resources said it was investigating where the entanglement occurred and whether it happened in Philippine waters or farther out at sea.

This tragic discovery highlights the danger of discarded waste in our oceans. Diapers, plastics, and ropes can entangle marine animals and damage the reefs they depend on.

Our oceans are not garbage dumps. Every piece of waste we dispose of improperly can become a threat to marine life.

A loggerhead sea turtle and a dolphin were reportedly found dead along Bagdad Beach in Tamaulipas, Mexico, after the November 13 SpaceX Starship booster explosion over the Gulf of Mexico.

Environmental group Conibio Global raised concerns after suspected rocket fragments began washing ashore near the beach. The discovery of the marine animals has prompted questions about the possible impact on wildlife.

Marine life deserves protection from pollution and environmental hazards—whether they come from land, sea, or space.

A NEW CONCERN FOR THE OCEAN'S GENTLE GIANTS. 🐋

The U.S. Navy has sought authorization to conduct training and testing using low-frequency active sonar across parts of the western and central North Pacific and eastern Indian Ocean.

The powerful underwater sound can disturb marine mammals, potentially disrupting behaviors such as feeding, migration, and communication.

UPDATE: NOAA Fisheries issued a seven-year authorization in July 2026, effective from August 2026 through August 2033. The authorization includes monitoring, reporting, and mitigation requirements for the Navy's activities.

Even when military training is considered necessary, protecting whales and other marine mammals from harmful underwater noise must remain a priority.

“THE HOSTAGES HAD ALREADY DUG THEIR OWN GRAVES. THEN DELTA FORCE KICKED DOWN THE DOORS.” — The Heroism of Medal of Honor Recipient SGM Thomas “Patrick” Payne.

In October 2015, intelligence reports confirmed that ISIS was preparing to mass-execute more than 70 Iraqi hostages held at a heavily fortified prison compound in Hawija, Kirkuk Province, Iraq. Freshly dug mass graves were already visible on satellite imagery.

Delta Force operator Sergeant Major (then SFC) Thomas "Patrick" Payne deployed on a daring joint helicopter night assault alongside Kurdish Counter Terrorism Group (CTG) forces to pull off one of the largest hostage rescues in modern special operations history:

Under immediate heavy machine-gun fire upon landing, Delta Force Master Sergeant Joshua Wheeler was mortally wounded leading the opening charge. Payne’s team breached the first compound, clearing the structure and liberating 38 hostages.

Hearing radio calls that a second assault team was pinned down at a fortified, burning building, Payne sprinted across an exposed courtyard through a barrage of enemy fire. He scaled a ladder to the roof, engaging barricaded ISIS fighters with grenades while enemy suicide vests detonated below him.

Moving to the ground floor as flames consumed the structure, Payne grabbed bolt cutters and repeatedly charged into the thick, toxic smoke under point-blank gunfire. Overcome by smoke and heat, he exited to catch his breath, re-entered multiple times, and finally sheared the master lock off the reinforced steel door, releasing 37 more trapped hostages.

Even after the roof began to collapse and the final evacuation order was radioed, Payne re-entered the burning inferno one last time to ensure every single hostage and teammate was safely out.

In total, 75 hostages were saved. On September 11, 2020, SGM Payne was awarded the Medal of Honor—becoming the first living Delta Force operator to receive the nation’s highest military decoration since the Battle of Mogadishu in 1993, and the first Medal of Honor recipient of Operation Inherent Resolve.

The sun is going down over the Mojave, and the jump hasn't started yet. On 18 July 2025, Marines with 2d Reconnaissance Battalion, 2d Marine Division, got ready for a night free-fall jump at the Marine Corps Air-Ground Combat Center in Twentynine Palms, California, during Service Level Training Exercise 4-25.

Most of a free-fall jump happens on the ground. Before anyone boards the C-130, rigs get checked and rechecked, straps are adjusted, oxygen systems are inspected, and the numbers that will decide where every jumper lands get worked out and verified. At night, over the desert, there's no room for mistakes. Everyone has to trust their own rig, the man packing next to them, and the team in the back of the aircraft.

That's the side of Recon most people never see. The skill that gets a team behind the lines quietly is built on hours of unglamorous preparation like this. The jump itself is the shortest part of the night.

Twenty-three years ago this Thanksgiving, about 600 soldiers from the 1st Armored Division and the 82nd Airborne Division sat down for turkey and ham at the Bob Hope Dining Facility at Baghdad International Airport. None of them knew who their guest of honor would be.

President George W. Bush had flown into Baghdad under darkness and tight secrecy. Almost no one outside a small circle knew about it, including most of the White House press corps. When he stepped out from behind a curtain, the room erupted. "I was just looking for a warm meal somewhere," he told them. Then he helped serve dinner and shook hands down the line. For decades, there were plans to retire the M2 Bradley. In 2026, the US-made armored vehicle is in higher demand than ever, and that has created an unusual engineering challenge: keeping the fleet running.

The problem is that many of the Bradley's components are simply no longer manufactured. The US Army's contracting command at Detroit Arsenal points to an aging manufacturing base, with original suppliers having long since stopped making several subsystems, things like turret drive control units, transmission control modules, targeting-system components, and other specialized electrical and structural parts unique to this version of the vehicle.

So the Army has put out a call to American industry: find companies that either still have these obsolete parts or can credibly restart production, refurbish the vehicles to a fully mission-capable standard, and help train Ukrainian mechanics to maintain them. The plan is to get each vehicle running and roadworthy first so it can ship quickly, with the harder-to-source parts handled afterward.

It's a reminder that keeping proven equipment in service isn't just about the machines, it's about the supply chains and the people behind them. Even as the Army develops the future XM30 to eventually take its place, the old Bradley is proving hard to let go of.

The Navy has confirmed its newest aircraft carrier will keep its name: the USS Doris Miller. "There is no intention to change the name," a spokesperson for the Navy secretary said.

The name matters. Doris Miller was the grandson of enslaved people, born to sharecroppers in rural Texas, who joined the Navy in 1939 after struggling to find work in the Jim Crow South. Like most Black sailors of that era, he was confined to the messman branch, cooking and cleaning, and barred from other roles.

On Dec. 7, 1941, Miller was doing laundry aboard the USS West Virginia when the first torpedo struck at Pearl Harbor. With his battle station flooded, he helped carry his mortally wounded captain to shelter, then manned an anti-aircraft machine gun he had never been trained to use and fired it until the ammunition ran out. "It wasn't hard," he said the next year. "I just pulled the trigger and she worked fine." He was among the last men to leave the ship. For his actions he received the Navy Cross, becoming the first Black American to be so honored.

CVN-81, still under construction in Newport News, Virginia, will be the first US aircraft carrier named for a Black American and the first named for an enlisted sailor. The confirmation follows reports earlier this year that the ship might be renamed, which drew a strong reaction from Miller's descendants. There are also ongoing efforts in Congress to upgrade his Navy Cross to the Medal of Honor.

Fair winds, Doris Miller. A name worth keeping.

Delta Force operator Sergeant Major (then SFC) Thomas "Patrick" Payne deployed on a daring joint helicopter night assault alongside Kurdish Counter Terrorism Group (CTG) forces to pull off one of the largest hostage rescues in modern special operations history:

Moving to the ground floor as flames consumed the structure, Payne grabbed bolt cutters and repeatedly charged into the thick, toxic smoke under point-blank gunfire. Overcome by smoke and heat, he exited to catch his breath, re-entered multiple times, and finally sheared the master lock off the reinforced steel door, releasing 37 more trapped hostages.

Even after the roof began to collapse and the final evacuation order was radioed, Payne re-entered the burning inferno one last time to ensure every single hostage and teammate was safely out.

In total, 75 hostages were saved. On September 11, 2020, SGM Payne was awarded the Medal of Honor—becoming the first living Delta Force operator to receive the nation’s highest military decoration since the Battle of Mogadishu in 1993, and the first Medal of Honor recipient of Operation Inherent Resolve.

Circling overhead in Super Six Two, Delta Force sniper team leader Master Sgt. Gary Gordon and his partner Sgt. 1st Class Randy Shughart watched armed hostile crowds numbering in the thousands converge on the downed wreckage. With no ground rescue convoy capable of reaching the site in time, Gordon radioed command requesting permission to be inserted on foot to protect the wounded crew. Command denied the request twice, warning that two men could not survive against an entire armed city. On their third urgent request, knowing rescue was hours away, command relented and cleared them for insertion

Fierce Defense And The Final Weapon Infilled roughly 100 meters away, Gordon and Shughart fought their way through an intense maze of shanties under heavy fire to reach the wreckage. They pulled Durant, who had sustained a broken leg and crushed vertebrae, from the crushed cockpit alongside his crew, moving them behind the fuselage to establish a perimeter. Fighting with bolt-action sniper rifles and sidearms, both snipers held off waves of militia until their ammunition ran dry. After Shughart fell, Gordon salvaged a rifle with the remaining rounds, handed it to the injured pilot with the parting words, “Good luck,” and went back into the fight with only his sidearm until he was overwhelmed

First Medals Of Honor Since Vietnam The stand of Gordon and Shughart delayed the armed crowd long enough to keep Durant alive until he was taken prisoner and ultimately released 11 days later. We were out of ammunition resupplies, Spanish military forces inside had barricaded themselves below, and we knew if they breached the courtyard walls, we were going to be lynched and burned.”

“In that moment, fear disappears. You stop worrying about dying, lock your focus down to your optic, and decide that every single round left in your mags is taking an enemy down with you.”

The eight-man team manned the rooftop parapets for hours under non-stop direct fire, repelling wave after wave of militia assaults attempting to breach the perimeter gates.

The Warrior Mindset Under Siege: When survival looks impossible, combat psychology shifts from panic to cold, lethal execution—focusing strictly on fundamentals and making every pull of the trigger count.

The Ultimate Stand: Gary Gordon And Randy Shughart At Super Six Four
The Radio Requests From Above On October 3, 1993, during the intense street fighting of the Battle of Mogadishu, Black Hawk helicopter Super Six Four, piloted by Chief Warrant Officer Michael Durant, was struck by an RPG and crashed into a hostile neighborhood. Circling overhead in Super Six Two, Delta Force sniper team leader Master Sgt. Gary Gordon and his partner Sgt. 1st Class Randy Shughart watched armed hostile crowds numbering in the thousands converge on the downed wreckage. With no ground rescue convoy capable of reaching the site in time, Gordon radioed command requesting permission to be inserted on foot to protect the wounded crew. Command denied the request twice, warning that two men could not survive against an entire armed city. On their third urgent request, knowing rescue was hours away, command relented and cleared them for insertion

Fierce Defense And The Final Weapon Infilled roughly 100 meters away, Gordon and Shughart fought their way through an intense maze of shanties under heavy fire to reach the wreckage. They pulled Durant, who had sustained a broken leg and crushed vertebrae, from the crushed cockpit alongside his crew, moving them behind the fuselage to establish a perimeter. Fighting with bolt-action sniper rifles and sidearms, both snipers held off waves of militia until their ammunition ran dry. After Shughart fell, Gordon salvaged a rifle with the remaining rounds, handed it to the injured pilot with the parting words, “Good luck,” and went back into the fight with only his sidearm until he was overwhelmed

First Medals Of Honor Since Vietnam The stand of Gordon and Shughart delayed the armed crowd long enough to keep Durant alive until he was taken prisoner and ultimately released 11 days later. On May 23, 1994, both snipers were posthumously awarded the Medal of Honor, becoming the first service members to receive the nation’s highest military decoration since the Vietnam War

At 32,000 feet over Pennsylvania, an ordinary Tuesday morning flight suddenly became every aviator’s worst nightmare.

A metal fatigue fracture inside the left CFM56 engine sheared off a fan blade at cruising speed. Within milliseconds, the entire cowling disintegrated into flying shrapnel, puncturing the fuselage and blowing out a cabin window at row 14.

The cockpit erupted into instant chaos. Rapid decompression roared through the airframe, dropping cabin temperature below zero, flooding the cockpit with white vapor, and filling the air with deafening wind noise. The Boeing 737 shuddered violently, banking hard to 41 degrees with only one operational engine and zero internal communication back to the flight attendants.

In command was Captain Tammie Jo Shults, backed by First Officer Darren Ellisor.

Decades before flying commercial routes, Shults was breaking barriers in naval aviation as one of the first women to pilot the supersonic F/A-18 Hornet and fly tactical profiles in the A-7 Corsair II. She had spent years mastering emergency procedures on pitching carrier decks in pitch darkness, conditioning her nervous system to replace fear with immediate muscle memory.

While cockpit alarms blared and the airframe fought severe aerodynamic drag, Shults keyed her microphone to Philadelphia air traffic control. Her voice did not crack. Her cadence did not waver. She sounded like someone ordering a morning coffee.

"Southwest 1380 has an engine fire," she transmitted calmly. "We would like to descend."

When the controller asked whether the aircraft was actively on fire, her reply was cold steel.

"No, it is not on fire, but part of it is missing. They say there is a hole and someone went out."

Wrestling asymmetric thrust and flap damage, Shults manually stabilized the crippled airliner, brought it down on runway 27L at 165 knots, and safely delivered 148 souls home.

In the face of danger, most would run toward safety. Yet, when then-Lance Cpl. Corbin was faced with such a decision, he ran toward peril and possible death – braving intense enemy fire to help injured comrades.

Corbin, a medium tactical vehicle replacement driver, and his unit were stationed in the Al Anbar province to help secure and stabilize the volatile area. They had just finished several days of routine patrol on May 7, 2005, and were returning to the Haditha Dam when they got the call.

A platoon from their battalion was under attack on the east side of the Euphrates River and needed support to block the insurgents' retreat. Corbin's team – a quick reaction force (QRF) – quickly responded to the call. As the QRF crept toward the attack site, there was an unnatural stillness in the air.

“There was no one out, nothing moving,” Corbin later told the Marine Corps Times.

With every nerve on alert, the QRF kept driving toward the ambush site, knowing there were injured Marines that needed them. Suddenly, a vehicle laden with IEDs sped toward the convoy and blew up between two of the Humvees. Another blast followed as enemy fighters began firing upon the group.

The swift attack devastated Corbin's team – three of the four vehicles were severely damaged, and 11 of 16 Marines were injured or killed. Taking control of the situation, Corbin immediately repositioned his vehicle between the insurgents' fire and the wounded Marines. As he radioed in the situation, he began directing a counter-attack.

As those that could return fire, Corbin began recovering dead and wounded personnel and moving them toward safety. Running through the line of fire, Corbin grabbed his wounded patrol leader and threw him over his shoulder. He then sprinted back to his Humvee, firing at enemies as he ran. Corbin ran back and forth several times through the kill zone, moving everyone he could out of the withering fire and loaded them into his vehicle.

Arming every able Marine with as much ammunition and weapons as they could hold, Corbin drove his severely damaged Humvee through the kill zone toward the battle aid station. Even injured, the Marines were a deadly force to be reckoned with. Insurgents continued to pelt the rumbling truck with mortars and small-arms fire, but the Marines made it to safety.

Corbin's quick actions ensured that no Marines were killed after that initial attack. For his leadership, Corbin was awarded the Navy Cross on April 12, 2006.

On April 4, 2004, the holy city of Najaf, Iraq erupted into chaos as Muqtada al-Sadr’s Mahdi Army launched a coordinated uprising against coalition forces.

“The Mahdi Army had completely encircled the compound. We were on the roof eight guys with small arms and precision rifles looking out at hundreds, if not thousands, of armed insurgents advancing down the streets. You could literally hear the roar of the crowd before the firing started. When they opened up, the air filled with RPGs, mortars, and PKM rounds chewing up the parapet walls.”

“Brass was piling up past our ankles. I was on my precision rifle engaging targets one after another, working the bolt so fast that the barrel was smoking. At one point, I looked over at the guys next to me. We were out of ammunition resupplies, Spanish military forces inside had barricaded themselves below, and we knew if they breached the courtyard walls, we were going to be lynched and burned.”

“In that moment, fear disappears. You stop worrying about dying, lock your focus down to your optic, and decide that every single round left in your mags is taking an enemy down with you.”

The eight-man team manned the rooftop parapets for hours under non-stop direct fire, repelling wave after wave of militia assaults attempting to breach the perimeter gates.

The Warrior Mindset Under Siege: When survival looks impossible, combat psychology shifts from panic to cold, lethal execution—focusing strictly on fundamentals and making every pull of the trigger count.
